correctness.rationale: Incidence columns for tree edges form an integral basis of A_{n-1}; reduced determinants ±1 give lattice equivalence and Cauchy–Binet determinant n, so equal intrinsic volume. The support function is max edge |x_i−x_j|. Project i.i.d. normal coordinates onto sum-zero H and separate the independent radial chi_{n-1} variable to obtain the exact Gaussian width formula. For the lower bound select a fixed neighbor of the |Z_i| maximum; condition on the maximizing index/magnitude and use truncated half-normal domination to bound neighbor expectation by sqrt(2/pi). Gaussian mgf of 2(n-1) variance-two signed increments bounds the upper maximum by 2sqrt(log(2n-2)); independent disjoint path edges reach it. Stars reach sqrt(2log n). A broom with n^alpha handle has scaled max 2sqrt(alpha) for alpha≥1/2, and an integrated union-tail E[M²]≤4log(2n)+4 guarantees uniform integrability for expectations, yielding all constants 4sqrt(alpha).

originality.rationale: D’Alì–Delucchi–Michałek Example 2.3 already proves tree root polytopes are lattice crosspolytopes, and Kabluchko–Litvak–Zaporozhets supply the generic Gaussian mean-width representation. Neither yields the graph-indexed edge-difference extremal **limit-set** over all trees. A Resultary finding on tree graphical zonotopes gives width variance for Minkowski sums; those are different from the convex-hull root polytopes (max vs sum of absolute differences), so it cannot imply this theorem.
